english: Entering the AR Trading Company greets you with a blinding sight.
A celestial being, wrought in radiant light.
Ah, Cleric. Arriving exactly when I need you.
This is the ambassador of the Golden Horde.
The light reaches out to you, as a voice forms in your mind.
Do not fear the light.
Ours do not dis-align. You are safe.
Your legs turn to jelly.
Your stomach yells.
This whole be not afraid business is sort of counter-productive, really.
Do the proper greeting. Title, and bow your head.
Greetings, celestial.
Ambassador. (Bow your head.)
Oh gods save me.
Cleric.
Trust me. That is what we wish.
The light flutters.
Snell stands behind you, clearly uncomfortable.
Careful, Cleric.
Beside the light stands a woman draped in red.
The light reaches towards her.
She bows her head to it.
Yes, Ambassador.
She begins to leave for the door- but on the way she throws you a stern glance.
You again.
Watch yourself, Cleric. For the Light watches you.
Once the ambassador's servant leaves, Viira lifts her chin, squinting. "So. We've been talking about some new projects on Waterlane. "
I mentioned how you helped getting the AEFAs out to local entrepreneurs. And they-
We know who you are.
We know who you are. Ragn and Snell.
The voice interrupts Viira, who immediately goes silent.
The goblin jolts at the mention of his name in his mind.
He dares not look at the light.
That's scary.
Of course you do. I'm a big deal.
...Okay.
Don't worry. The ambassador means it in a nice way.
Agent Viira snickers to herself.
The ambassador's light then turns to your companion.
A goblin in service of The Dragon of Tolstad.
Uh.
You tread a clean path. You led the front during the Icebay Point operation.
You stabilized the HWBT City Below expansion project on your first year of service.
A goblin going against the grain to get results.
You have been noticed.
(Look at Snell.)
<shake>Uh</shake>.
Snell attempts to glare at the light.
He is sweating.
Snell is nervous. You feel bad for him.
Stand up to the light, goblin.
Do not falter.
Thanks for... noticing.
The light grows closer to you.
You are special, Ragn. An exception.
The Horde places attention on exceptions. That is what we do.
How am I special?
I'm special.
(Just squint at the light.)
You are the only registered cleric in the city who is not listed in the Party of Norvik.
That's just because they didn't like you.
A bureaucratic mess.
Because they suck. Duh.
You have a history of political violence. You have an innate talent for the esoteric arts.
Well, yes. You are potentially the greatest wizard of this generation.
Yes. You are the greatest wizard of this generation. Obviously.
That was a false report. You did not enact any violence.
The violence was enacted upon you. By an Urthguard soldier.
Violence? No. You are not capable of that.
You didn't even throw any rocks.
Plus, that was years ago. Why is the celestial bringing this up?
You have shown support of Reedsian ideologues in public writing. Multiple times.
Yeah. Your patriarch did NOT like that.
Not one bit.
That was a mistake. A stumble into the dark side of politics.
You have paid for it dearly.
The only reason why you haven't been fired is your incredible magical knowledge.
Yeah. They only keep you around because you're still useful.
Otherwise, with all this bullshit hanging about, you'd be gone a long time ago.
You are an anomaly, Ragn.
What you have done here with Agent Viira shows more proof of that.
Why are you paying any attention to me?
Thank you. (Take a deep bow.)
Stop looking into me. I don't like you Golden Horde people.
It is what we do.
Cleric.
Perhaps you will reconsider.
The Golden Horde wishes to extend a bond of service to you.
You and Snell.
A bond...? he mutters behind you.
Could be cool. But what do you get out of it?
Your bond is to this city. Nothing else.
And to Urth, right?
Oh. Yes. To Urth as well.
A bond.
That could be interesting.
What do I get in return?
I'm not interested.
A fair question, Ragn.
Hear the ambassador out, Cleric.
She is trying to help you not make a fool out of yourself.
She's in his pocket.
The Golden Horde offers many opportunities for outside contractors.
Addressed through the Askanii-Reeds Trading Company, we would be very interested in building this potential relationship.
This means, for you: well-paid positions of power. Political ambitions. Monetary security.
In return, this means: Monthly communications with agents. Occasional alternate goals as ordained by us - and eventually joining the Golden Horde's outreach program.
In short, become their spy.
In return, they protect you.
Safety under the WING of the HORDE.
Until you're no longer useful.
This would be signing your soul away to a foreign power.
If calculated, it could prove useful. But in the long-term, it seems foolish.
This celestial wants to use you. They view you as sheep. Nothing else.
You cannot read this celestial. It is truly alien to you.
The AR Trading Co. would of course cooperate on such a deal. If you were interested, Cleric.
We have deep ties with the Golden Horde, as you can imagine.
Is this offer something you would be interested in, Ragn?
Potentially.
Yes. Sign me up.
No. Never.
I'm not sure. Can I think about it?
Yes. You may. Perhaps we shall speak again on this. In the future.
Nothing about this has to happen right away...
His response has been recorded. That is what we needed.
We shall leave this for now.
We shall be in contact.
And while we are here, the offer is also extended to Snell.
Do you hold any interest in this deal?
His eyes dart to you.
He is being clever here. Calculated.
I can consider it.
Your consideration has been recorded.
He shrugs.
Thank you.
Now, to move on.
Several AEFAs have been signed on Tolstad. That is good work, Agent Viira.
Oh, like I mentioned, the Cleric's effort was integral to this success.
And we will continue in the coming days, post-election.
That is satisfactory.
Yeah, I gave out those contracts to a bunch of people.
Not so many were positive about this AEFA business.
We'll get everyone into the Accord, eventually.
Oh yes. We heard back from several of them.
They'll come around.
They always do.
Oh yes!
As to the content of these contracts, I have been informed of some changes.
Changes?
Her stance changes.
She did not like that.
Uh oh.
What changes?
Currently the Accord has a big incentive for Reedsian investors. We wish to expand that to include those of the Golden Horde.
I believe we spoke about this at the-
This AEFA also includes several loopholes and problematic elements that could interfere with the Golden Horde's current and future blockades.
The Clanlands.
Yes. Among others.

If local businesses are able to trade freely via land, as well as sea, to regions and states the Golden Horde deems sanctioned, in both more serious cases as the Clanland conflict, as well as lesser situations of targeted tariffs, then we cannot move forward.
This issue has been brought forth already with your owners. Expect several errata in the near future.
It would have been good to see these comments before the election. As discussed.
I apologize for the tardiness. But I assure you, this issue is entirely the fault of the Askanii-Reeds Trading Company.
Hah!
This guy just said, I'm sorry, but everything is actually your fault to her face.
These celestials are hilarious.
The rage.
She clenches her jaw as she stares at him.
Agent Viira.
This is above you.
Above her rank.
In the clouds. With the angels.
She clears her throat and straightens her outfit.
Of course.
Of course, Ambassador. Thank you for the heads up.
Her entire being is restrained rage.
The light turns back to you.
The Golden Horde is very interested in seeing economic prosperity in your city, Ragn.
So they can use us as slave labor.
They want control.
Growth through foreign economic influence is not true growth.
If Norvik owes its economic stability to foreign powers, those powers shall be its true owners.
It's an intelligent strategic move, if you wish to control your neighbors.
Agent Viira nods, looking like she's going to explode.
The first step towards that, is handling the Clanlands. For far too long Norvik has ignored its halfling war criminal populace.
I ask you, Ragn, as a cleric of this city: do you believe the humans will choose prosperity over the propaganda of the Clanlands?
Viira says nothing, but throws you a glance.
Her anger now fades, replaced by another expression.
Her eyes telling you: this guy's a monster, so be careful.
You're not sure what it means. But it is a strained expression.
What are the halflings to us?
Oh gods. What should I say?
They are our closest neighbors. The Urthfolk will always stand by the Clanlands. (Stand by the Clanlands.)
The people of Norvik do not believe in halfling propaganda. (Stand by the Golden Horde.)
My city does not involve itself in foreign conflicts. We will simply seek prosperity and avoid propaganda. (Stay neutral.)
Neighbors. Not too close.
Some type of neighbors.
Just another folktype. Unlike dwarves, they have no close bond with the Urthfolk.
They are a resilient, stout folk, one found all across the Coast.
Not too unlike humans, they have been enslaved and controlled for most of their history.
You must stand by them.
Careful now.
If you antagonize this guy, you've got a whole new mess to deal with.
Maybe just stay neutral.
If you kiss his ass, he'll know you're an asset.
If you go all halfling lovey-dovey, he'll know you'll never be one.
But considering the weird tension here, that might not be a bad thing. If you antagonize him, you might be able to push back.
Which, if you do it correctly... might net you some points with Agent Viira.
Who cares about the halflings?
But more importantly, while this guy is clearly not someone to fuck with- if you push back in just the right way...
For now.
Ominous.
Good.
The light perceives you.
The Golden Line is set.
Halflings have shown themselves unable to accept this fact.

We set the Line to protect them. To create a lasting peace. Since they refuse to comply with our reasonable demands - I hope you understand - our most peaceful method of handling their terrorism is through sanctions.
The light turns back to Viira.
Agent Viira. You have been a valuable asset for many years. Yet I sense frustration in you. That is not acceptable.
She glares at the light.
You will make certain the Askanii-Reeds Trading Company fully complies with the AEFA erratum.
It is a matter of Golden Horde security. It is not negotiable. It will be your highest priority as of now.
If the Cleric is agreeable, funds will be procured for his involvement as well.
Viira looks defeated.
The orc is beaten.
This is tense.
Horrific. This celestial wields enormous power in those words of his.
Both the Freestriders and this monster can go fall through every hell in the book!
This is the power of a god. It's almost as if you have to kneel...
He's so precise in his words- you have no chance here.
Focus.
The light-guy is fast and precise- but you know. You KNOW that he's bullshitting. It's INSTINCT.
Catch him on it. For the Revolution. Stand up to him first, then do it!
Catch the ambassador in a contradiction.
I am happy to see the Golden Horde helping my city, Ambassador. (Kiss his ass.)
I understand. (Stay neutral.)
This is all bullshit. The Freestriders are corrupt. The Golden Horde are a bunch of monsters. I can't stand either of you. (Don't side with either. Fuck 'em.)
Viira perks up at your words.
The light watches you. Not saying anything at first.
Then the voice emits one word:
Mortal.
Decaying. Flawed.
I see you. The light grows. "As you are."
He's giving you a chance to back down.
Don't!
I am happy to hear that.
And just saying, I totally support the invasion of the Fordnip Commonwealth. Those halflings had it coming! (Kiss it harder.)
Your presence is a blessing in these dark times. (Kiss it slightly less egregiously.)
The Golden Line.
You'd think an all-powerful angel-horde would be able to do whatever they want.
Instead, they draw a line in the sand. Why?
Well, you know why.
International pressure.
Exactly.
They can't just invade Askanii, since that'd make every country on the Coast pull the alarms.
You see how he pushes for the image that we need them- but not the other way around?
Poke on that! Now!
Ambassador. If you want to solve your Clanlands-problem, then you need support from the international community. You need the Free Cities' support.
The light flickers.
This is a cooperation. You know the Revolution will be hurt, as will your ambitions, if they push too hard on the AEFAs.
The ambassador perceives you.
Make concessions, Ambassador. It's worth it. You know the local Freestriders will rout and dance around it if you don't. Make sure your Choir knows it.
You speak with confidence, Ragn.
Only because you know I am correct.
The Golden Line. The Horde and its invasion.
You know he's bullshitting you on some level...
But about WHAT?
(Stare at the Ambassador's light.)
No. No, no, no.
No way you'll get it in time. You've been staring at him for like, three seconds at this point.
YOU GOTTA SAY SOMETHING!
ANYTHING!
What should I say?!
Just... be nice. Calm. Normal.
That should solve it, in a somewhat peaceful manner.
No.
You should tell them both to leave you alone.
If you want to be smart, then just stay neutral.
Lashing out will only cause people to hate you now. Don't want that.
This celestial is a monster.
You do not owe them anything.
I... I will take this into... consideration. (Bow your head deeply and neutrally.)
Fuck the Freestriders! Fuck the Golden Horde! I despise you both. (Yell, and break your ties with the Freestriders.)
Good, the voice says.
The Golden Horde is glad to be of assistance to your people, Ragn.
Viira closes her eyes and sighs.
The light intensifies.
You speak from the heart.
Fascinating.
We will however not be interested in working with you going forward.
Agent Viira, I question your judgment here as well. I assume you understand this.
Yes, Ambassador, she grunts, her jaw clenched and eyes locked at you.
Fire and brimstone.
I apologize for this.
The light retracts, focused in on the head of the celestial.
Viira looks on with a smirk, clearly entertained.
Oh yeah.
You hit the right spot.
The AEFA erratum is not my decision, the voice says.
However, I will consider your statement, he says. "Agent Viira. Do you concur?"
I do, Ambassador. My earlier frustration was due to this problematic situation. The AR leadership will struggle with these changes.
A... compromise would go through much easier. Even just starting with a discussion - perhaps between you and our owners - would go a long way.
Good. This will be taken into account.
The ambassador begins to float towards the door.
I will leave you now. Thank you for your time.
The radiant light-being opens the door via some type of telekinesis and floats out onto the streets of Waterlane.
Viira stands up, walking over to the fireplace, leaning against the brickwork.
She lets out a deep sigh.
Good going. You handled that well.
Didn't mean to toss you in like that, but the ambassador insisted.
No problem. I can handle anything.
That was horrifying.
Yeah, screw you for that.
Confident as always.
A bit, yeah.
She laughs.
Guess I deserve it.
Let me tell you, we're not quite as owned by the Golden Horde as that sounded like.
It's a functional cooperation. They don't exactly live our libertarian values.
Celestials do have a tendency for the authoritarian. And the... supremacist.
Gods.
I thought you would have a bit more tact.
You were mistaken.
I don't want anything to do with this.
I'm sorry.
I'm not sorry.
<shake>Obviously</shake>.
I don't care.
She slams her clenched fist into the wall.
Not so hard to cause any self-harm, but hard enough to make a sound.
An act of frustration.
Please leave, Cleric.
Now.
E-...Maybe I should.
She lets out a deep, tired groan.
Viira is allowing herself to be herself around you, a little bit more.
I don't want to congratulate you on annoying our dear friend the ambassador, but...
The orc agent shoots you an intriguing smirk. The type you haven't seen for many, many years.
That was fucking beautiful.
Moving closer, she follows it up with a firm tap on the back.
I really tossed you into the deep end, but you handled yourself exactly the way I like...
(Gulp.) "I'm happy to be of service."
That's how we Freestriders deal with imperialists.
It was slightly horrifying.
I just told the truth to the celestial bastard.
So service-minded...
Yes, indeed...
How do you think I feel?
You sure did...
Look, I have to deal with the Choir entanglement all the time. And they never cease with the bullshit.
Having a third party - that's you - push back for once? Absolutely glorious to watch.
I thank you for that. Personally. And... professionally too, of course.
The orc looks at you, relief in her eyes.
This, along with all the help on the AEFAs- I owe you some type of reward, don't I?
Oh! This is the right moment: Ask for an advance.
Or hell, allude to some kind of payment for delivering the AEFAs.
A reward?
It's time to step up. ASK HER OUT.
You have already been promised a DATE with this handsome woman. That is reward enough.
How about some money?
A reward sounds nice.
I don't need a reward.
Such a gentleman.
She gives you a thoughtful expression for a few seconds.
...Yes. That is what I said.
She is choosing her words carefully.
She likes it! Go for the big one!
I love you.
How about a date?
You and me. Dinner. Some day next week.
You see her close her eyes in shame.
You're breaking her.
The poor woman.
I mean- I, I...
Viira glares at you.
...I love you.
...How about dinner?
She rubs her eyes.
I appreciate the gesture, Cleric. But perhaps we should get to know each other first.
How about dinner?
Dinner.
A date.
The orc looks at you, a contemplative look on her face.
Okay. Let's do it.
YES!
You are a successful man now.
Congratulations. You're proud of you.
Sounds good.
Dinner!
(Hold back tears.) "Okay."
But perhaps something more... tangible would also be fitting.
Hmm...
I've got something better in mind.
It does, doesn't it?
Oh, don't be so humble. You deserve something.
Agent Viira glances along the room.
For one, I'll be sure to grant you full access to the rest of the facilities, if you wanted to investigate the Warehouse properly.
A bit late for that.
But beyond that...
Well... you see, we have this sword here.
It's called Kattegatt.
She approaches the massive Zweihânder, propped up on the wall.
As she places her hand upon the grip of the sword, you see something curious happen.
It curls up.
A cursed blade.
Ah. It's a selective blade.
It doesn't like you?
Interesting.
As she removes her hand from the blade, it un-rolls itself immediately.
A fickle weapon. Ever heard of such a thing?
It was purchased years ago, from an excavation in Reeds. Old Arcanist cache- a Coast War armory.
It's Vorpal. Extremely magical, with perfect metallic endurance and sharpness.
It would be worth half a fortune, somewhere up to fifty thousand crowns - if not for the fact that it refuses to be used.
It simply rolls itself up when wielded by anyone, in any way.
Come. Try it.
(Touch the grip.)
Just like with Viira's touch, yours also causes it to roll up.
It's quite funny. However, I've had comments from upper staff that it's quite embarrassing to have spent money on it. So I've been tasked with making it go away.
It's not the most useful weapon- but if you're interested, you could take it as a reward for your work.
It is still quite magical. Maybe even sentient, considering the reaction.
Your scarf curls up when Viira doesn't notice, whispering in your ear.
Blade. Is. Thinking.
I'll take it! (Accept the sword.)
Nah. Give me something else. (Refuse.)
Meek recognizes type of blade. Old Master had one, once.
It will judge. Only work if happy.
Very cranky metal...
Great!
She hands you the Vorpal Sword in its curled up state.
Glad to see it come to use. Just don't tell anyone where you got it from.
The orc laughs loudly.
Understandable.
I was planning on handing you this magical sword we've been hoarding.
But unfortunately, I believe it has been misplaced. Or handed out by someone else.
She looks at the empty spot on the wall.
Whoops.
Well, since you already took Kattegatt, it's no matter. Maybe you'll just get some-
Let's get you some money instead.
She grabs a pouch from a drawer and tosses it your way.
Twelve hundred crowns. View it as a token of our appreciation.
Holy shit.
That is, on average, about four months rent.
Wow! She must really like you.
Beyond that, I'll also be sure to put in a good word- so we can work together again, post-election. Since I guarantee you...
There will be a lot of work to do.
Looking forward to it.
I'll consider it.
(Just nod.)
Great to hear.
Of course. You're busy. I understand.
She winks.
She nods back.
I've got some paperwork to deal with, but if there's anything else I can help with, just let me know.
Very happy to see you on our side, Cleric.
The tall orc woman gives you a warm smile.
(Bow your head.)
